key_insight: The paper argues that machine learning can augment classical iterative solvers for linear and nonlinear systems, improving efficiency while retaining the interpretability and reliability of traditional methods.
engineering_relevance: Hybrid iterative methods could make large-scale scientific and engineering simulations faster and more robust, especially where direct solvers are too costly and nonlinear convergence is challenging.
method: Combine classical iterative solvers with machine learning components
Use ML to tune hyperparameters, guide updates, or improve convergence behavior
Focus on both linear systems and nonlinear methods such as Newton-type solvers
evidence_signal: This is an overview paper, so the evidence comes from surveying state-of-the-art methods rather than reporting a single benchmark or dataset.
watch_item: Hybrid methods may be sensitive to problem class and training/validation conditions, so gains may not transfer reliably across different systems or initial guesses.
paper_title: An overview of machine learning-enhanced iterative methods for systems of linear and nonlinear equations
